description:
About the Position

KTH’s Hardware Security group is recruiting a doctoral student to investigate remote fault attacks on cryptographic implementations. The project examines how attackers can disrupt computation and how secure systems can detect or withstand those faults.

Research Position Overview

Develop and assess offensive and defensive methods, including machine-learning analysis of faulty behaviour and practical countermeasures. The project connects cryptographic implementation security with embedded systems and hardware-level experimentation.

Research Areas

  • Cryptographic implementation
  • Fault attacks
  • Security countermeasures

Funding and Duration

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionPhD researcher
SalaryMonthly salary under KTH’s doctoral-student salary agreement; the advert does not give an individual amount.
DurationFour years of full-time doctoral study. The initial employment period is normally no longer than one year, with renewals of up to two years; departmental duties may be up to 20%.
Programme / host supportSwedish Research Council-supported research in the Hardware Security group.
BenefitsEmployment benefits follow KTH’s applicable conditions; consult the notice for the contract and assessment rules.

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic preparation and appointment conditions
ComponentDetails
Applicant eligibilityWorldwide applicants may be considered subject to academic eligibility, recruitment checks and the stated appointment conditions.
Academic preparationRelevant second-cycle qualification, or at least 240 higher-education credits including 60 at second-cycle level, or equivalent preparation.
Research skillsCryptography, embedded systems, side-channel or fault analysis and machine learning. Hardware-security courses, a relevant thesis or publications strengthen the application.
LanguageEnglish meeting KTH’s English B/6 requirement or recognised equivalent.

Application dates

Recruitment dates and location
ComponentDetails
Recruitment statusOpen when verified against the official source
Deadline17 October 2026
Start dateNot specified in the vacancy.
LocationStockholm, Sweden

How to Apply

  • CV and motivation/research-interest letter of no more than two pages.
  • Degree certificates, transcripts and evidence of English eligibility, with required translations.
  • Relevant reports or publications; provide an abstract and link for longer documents.

Submit through the application system linked from the official vacancy. Follow its current document and translation instructions.

Selection and Contact

Selection follows the academic and professional criteria in the official notice.

Research contact: Elena Dubrova and Carl-Mikael Zetterling.

About KTH Royal Institute of Technology

KTH Royal Institute of Technology is based in Stockholm, Sweden. The advertised research group provides the academic setting for this appointment, alongside the school’s doctoral or research environment.
